items.title: Lisa Parrott interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 22, 2021
items.q: played some duets at a little art gallery in Brooklyn with my friend Jamie Fox

ctx.x: Well you’re directing me to a vaguely formed question and also connected with I believe this is a quote from Ornette Coleman, “There is a music that has the quality to preserve life.” And I wonder two things: what does music — what can music mean? And what do you hope an audience listening to your music will get out of it?

First of all I’m tearing up because I relate so much to this, and especially since I’ve just come off the back of barely playing with anybody for almost a year and a half. And before I left on this trip, in May I finally played some duets at a little art gallery in Brooklyn with my friend Jamie Fox. And we’re both vaccinated so we’ve both been getting together. He was the first person I didn’t wear a mask around, we were both like can we do this? I think we can. And then we actually played a gig for about ten…

with the musicians that the audience cannot help but be brought into that and also taken along for that experience. And I would hope that, I suppose if my Dad can come to one of my gigs where I’m playing heavy harmolodics [gestures air quotes] — I’m saying that in embedded commas because like some of it, my, was it two years ago or maybe three years ago, but one of my last times I was out here playing gigs Harry, the bass player, came and he was not expecting to like my music. And he was fascinated. He was like,…
